purpose: What the pinned Engineering Assurance mapping must answer for each case, stated before the run rather than read back from it.
derivation_rule: Every `derived` case is ONE named edit to the pinned release's own fixture bytes, re-derived by scripts/legacy_evidence_view.py at run time. A committed fixture that is not equal to its declared derivation is a failure, not a fixture: a hand-written blob can be made to fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the check under test.
control_rule: Every negative names the positive control it is paired with. A refusal never observed to accept anything is indistinguishable from a validator that refuses everything, and proves nothing about either.
discrimination: Each case is separated from the others by a field the view reports — outcome, source schema version, or source record id — and not by upstream free text alone.

cases.why: The pinned v1 release fixture, bound to its own digest. This is the positive control: the mapping reads it and does not refuse it.
The pinned v2 release fixture. A second positive control on the other schema branch, so a v1-only mapping cannot pass as complete.

One edit: schemaVersion set to a version the mapping has never seen. Must be `incompatible` — the bytes parsed, so this is not `unreadable`, and an unknown schema must never be treated as empty or current.
One edit: a recognised schema version with a required field removed. Read as far as the contract and refused there, which is a different finding from an unknown version.
One edit: historicalDisposition set to retracted. The record stays readable and its staleness is mapped as evidence state rather than making it disappear or read as a current pass.
One edit: the first third of the bytes. Truncation is the commonest real corruption and must not be read as an absent or empty record.
One edit: valid JSON that is not an object. Parseable is not the same as readable, and the mapping must say so.
